plan: With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the standard first-price auction equilibrium bid is value × (n-1)/n = 28 × 2/3 ≈ 18.7. This balances winning probability against profit margin, since bidding my full value would yield zero profit even if I win. I'll bid slightly below this theoretical optimum to account for uncertainty and secure positive expected profit while maintaining reasonable win probability.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the Nash equilibrium strategy in a first-price auction is to bid (n-1)/n of your value, i.e., 2/3 of value. This balances winning probability against overpaying. My value is $23, so optimal bid ≈ $15.30. This maximizes expected profit by shading appropriately given rivals also shade their bids similarly.

With values uniformly distributed on [0,49] and 3 bidders total, the optimal first-price auction bid shading factor is (n-1)/n = 2/3, assuming symmetric equilibrium strategies.
